findings.claim: A compact bridge-width correction improves held-out specimen load reconstruction over constant apparent-toughness and quadratic controls.
findings.equation:
With $x=a/W$ and $r=1-b/B$, the source-declared cantilever geometry factor is

$$
f(x)=1.46+24.36x-47.21x^2+75.18x^3,
\qquad \widehat P=\frac{BW^{3/2}}{L f(x)}(K_0+c r).
$$

Here K0=0.636134MPa sqrt(m) and c=5.430604MPa sqrt(m); geometry in micrometres yields force in mN. Full precision is in rules.json. These coefficients describe apparent geometric response at bridge failure; neither is claimed to be intrinsic silicon toughness.
findings.prior_art: See research_history/PRIOR_ART.json; broad physical relationships already published, no exhaustive novelty claim.
findings.falsification: The notch-only alternative worsens development MAE to0.02596mN and confirmation to0.02860mN, so relative notch depth alone does not replace bridge width in this task. A bounded regime model happens to score0.015961mN after opening confirmation, but its development error was worse and one boundary parameter was at its bound; it remains a diagnostic alternative rather than replacing the preselected reference. This disagreement is useful evidence for future independent experiments.
findings.scope: One wafer and post-test geometry; no intrinsic-toughness or prospective safety claim.
